title: Starship Flight 15: Ship 42 in orbit, booster diverted
seoTitle: Starship Flight 15: in orbit after launch, Saturday Ship catch still ahead
description: Starship Flight 15 lifted off 13 November 2026 from Starbase Pad 2. Super Heavy diverted to the Gulf. Ship 42 is in orbit with 26 Starlink V3s deployed, and a tower catch is still planned Saturday if systems stay healthy.
ogImageAlt: Starship Flight 15 title card on a dark background with the Supercharged Daily bolt
afterSub: Booster diverted. Ship 42 is coasting toward a Saturday catch if systems stay healthy. See the updates log.
featureGo: In orbit: the flight so far and Saturday's Ship catch →
summary: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Pad 2 at Starbase on Friday 13 November 2026 at about 4:47 p.m. CT (22:47 UTC), according to Space.com's live coverage of SpaceX's webcast. Super Heavy Booster 22 diverted to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf. NASASpaceflight, quoting SpaceX's Dan Huot, said the booster automatically aborted the Pad 2 return because of a guidance, navigation and control issue.

Ship 42 reached orbit — only the second Starship to do so — and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites. SpaceX said on 14 November at 05:44 UTC that the Ship and its heatshield were healthy and that a return-to-launch-site catch at Starbase was still planned about 22.5 hours after launch. That catch is still a go/no-go, not a result.

This will not be a dual catch. The tower has caught a Super Heavy booster three times, on Flights 5, 7 and 8; it has never caught a Ship. The remaining first is a Ship catch on Saturday, if systems stay healthy.

Alex R's 12 November minute-by-minute video — countdown to Saturday's Ship catch, using SpaceX's published times — is on the Ship 42 page and as a direct link under Where to watch. Actual Friday events ran about two minutes later than that window-open clock.

heatShield.lead: Bringing the Ship home intact means surviving re-entry, and that is the heat shield's job.

points.text: Thousands of small hexagonal tiles cover the Ship's windward side. Because the Ship is mostly a plain cylinder, most tiles can share one shape and the rest are machined to fit, CNBC reported in August 2021.
In a 2019 test SpaceX heated tiles to about 1,650 K (around 1,377 °C or 2,510 °F), its estimate of orbital re-entry temperature, Digital Trends reported.
Most tiles are attached mechanically rather than glued, and SpaceX makes them in-house, according to Air & Space (December 2021). The space shuttle's glued tiles needed long repairs between flights.

updates.text: SpaceX: Starship and its heatshield are healthy nearly seven hours after launch. Teams are still monitoring systems ahead of a planned return-to-launch-site catch at Starbase about 22.5 hours after launch.
Elon Musk: Starship is traveling around the world every ~90 minutes right now.
NASASpaceflight, quoting SpaceX's Dan Huot: continuing orbital flight with Ship 42. Booster 22 automatically aborted the attempt to return to Pad 2 due to a guidance, navigation and control issue.
SpaceX: payload deploy complete. All 26 Starlink V3 satellites are in orbit.
SpaceX: Starship performed its orbital insertion burn and entered orbit of Earth for the second time.
SpaceX: Super Heavy has diverted to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf.
SpaceX: liftoff of Starship. Space.com's live coverage of the webcast put T-0 at about 4:47 p.m. CT (22:47 UTC).

Alex R posted a minute-by-minute Flight 15 animation on X, using SpaceX's published timeline. If the window opens on time, the Ship catch is Saturday afternoon, about 22 and a half hours after Friday lift-off. Times are local Starbase (CST) and move if the launch slips.

Re-checked SpaceX's Flight 15 mission page on 13 Nov 2026: still as soon as Friday 13 November from Pad 2, 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC), 75-minute window, pending regulatory approval. Dual catch, 26 Starlink V3, more than 22 hours, webcast about 30 minutes before liftoff. This is a re-check, not a new date.

SpaceX: Ship 42 moved to the Starbase pad ahead of launch. The Flight 15 window is still as soon as Friday 13 November, 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC), 75 minutes, pending regulatory approval. Webcast about 30 minutes before liftoff. No FAA licence is published.
SpaceX lists Flight 15 as soon as Friday 13 November, 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC), 75-minute window, pending regulatory approval.

We checked this page against sources. The heat shield has thousands of tiles (CNBC), not a confirmed 18,000; the temperature is SpaceX's 2019 test figure (about 1,377 °C), not 1,400 °C; two unsourced claims (the gap-sealing felt and the tile factory's output) were removed; the booster-catch count (three) and the 14 orbits are now attributed.
